To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the particle size of Rh/SiO(2) catalysts affects the reactivity and selectivity in the CO/H-2/ethylene reaction.
propionaldehyde formation is enhanced on undercoordinated surface sites and that the presence of carbonyl species on Rh particles inhibits CO insertion into C2H4.
the reaction mechanism for propionaldehyde (CO insertion) is particle size dependent.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the investigation of the C2H4 + CO + H2 reaction over Rh/SiO(2) model catalyst surfaces.
understanding how the size of metal particles influences their reactivity in heterogeneous catalysis.

the development of new model catalysts and the investigation of the structure and reactivity of Rh nanoparticles under near atmospheric conditions, which will be of importance to the development of new heterogeneous catalysts for industrial use.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the observed particle size effects on propionaldehyde formation is due to the presence of undercoordinated Rh surface atoms, which are present at the surface of smaller particles, and the presence of Rh(CO) species on the surface, which is observed on smaller particles and correlates with a lower propionaldehyde formation.
Rh particle size has a significant impact on propionaldehyde production and that the observed particle size dependent activity is driven by the presence of Rh(CO)2 and Rh(CO)Hydride species.

the maximum activity in the C2H4/H2/CO reaction is observed on 2-3 nm Rh particles, and that the activity decreases on larger and smaller particles due to the formation of Rh carbonyls and the lack of Rh undercoordinated sites.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

Rh/SiO(2) catalysts exhibit a maximum activity for propionaldehydes production via CO insertion at 〈dp 〉 = 3.0 nm, which is attributed to a balance between the presence of undercoordinated Rh species and carbonyl hybrides on small particles and a lower density of undercoordinated sites on larger particles.
Rh particle size effects on propionaldehyde production are driven by the presence of undercoordinated Rh atoms and the presence of Rh hydride species.

the observed Rh particle size dependence for CO insertion is driven primarily by a decrease in the number of undercoordinated Rh surface sites as 〈dp 〉 increases, and secondarily by the presence of Rh(CO) species on smaller Rh particles.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the particle size dependence for CO insertion is not driven by a single factor, rather it is a result of the interplay between the presence of undercoordinated sites and Rh carbonyl hybride species on the Rh surface.
particle size dependent reactivity can arise due to a combination of site-specific and dispersion effects.
the observed Rh particle size dependence in the C2H4 + CO + H2 reaction is driven by the formation of carbonyl species on small particles, which are known to be active for CO insertion.
